**Russia was accused of sending tanks into Ukraine for the first time yesterday while the West’s attention was diverted by the chaos in Iraq.
The development threatens to destroy the tentative peace process just when the US and EU had hoped Vladimir Putin had agreed to ease tensions in the region.
Interior Minister Arseny Avakov claimed that Russian tanks crossed the border through a checkpoint controlled by pro-Russian separatists in the Luhansk region.
The separatists, who have seized control of several towns and cities in mainly Russian-speaking eastern Ukraine, were reportedly aided by the Russian military, according to Avakov.
"This is a direct violation of Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity," Avakov stated in a press conference.
"This blatant act of aggression cannot be ignored."
Moscow has denied any involvement with the separatists or sending military hardware into Ukraine.
"These claims are fabricated and designed to undermine the fragile peace process," a spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry declared.
This development comes at a sensitive time, with the US and EU striving to engage with Russia in dialogue to resolve the crisis.
Just weeks ago, President Putin had pledged to reduce border tensions and allow for greater autonomy within the eastern regions of Ukraine.
President Petro Poroshenko condemned the alleged incursion and called for an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council.
"This act of aggression will be met with a swift and decisive response," he warned.

sentences.sentence: ##  SpaceX Rocket Landing Delayed Again - Aiming for Tuesday
It’s set to be one of the most groundbreaking moments in humanity’s six decades of space exploration: Today SpaceX was due to land a rocket on a floating platform after launching.
But those looking forward to this pivotal moment will have to wait a little longer.
The launch of the Falcon 9 rocket, carrying a Dragon capsule, has been delayed once again due to an issue with one of the engines.
This marks the second delay for the mission, with an earlier attempt earlier this week also foiled by the same technical snag.
Now, SpaceX aims to launch at 11.18am GMT on Tuesday 6 January.
If successful, the mission will mark a historical achievement: the first-ever attempt to land a rocket booster on solid ground following launch.

After delivering the Dragon capsule to space, the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket will attempt to execute a controlled descent and touchdown on a specialized barge positioned in the Atlantic Ocean.
"This is a high-risk, high-reward endeavor," said CEO Elon Musk.
“We estimate the probability of success is around 50%."
Despite the uncertainty, SpaceX is committed to perfecting the reusable rocket technology.
The company’s long-term vision involves recovering and reusing rockets, significantly reducing the cost of space travel and opening new possibilities for space exploration.
The world is watching, eagerly anticipating the potential for a successful landing and the dawn of a new era in spaceflight.

sentences.sentence: ##  Hopes Fade as MH370 Mystery Deepens: Families Demand Answers
**New Zealanders Danica and Paul Weeks are no strangers to disaster.
The couple's eldest son, Lincoln, was born in the midst of an earthquake in Christchurch in 2010.

Just over three years later, in December 2013, they faced another terrifying ordeal when their younger son, Euan, was on board Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370, which disappeared without a trace over the Indian Ocean.
Days turned into weeks, and weeks into months, with each passing moment intensifying the agonizing uncertainty for Euan’s family and the families of the 239 other passengers.
Martial arts star Ju Kun was among those on board the fateful flight, leaving the global martial arts community reeling.
Tributes and messages of support are being shared online, forming a digital tapestry of grief and hope.
Communities around the world, from Kuala Lumpur to Wellington, are holding vigils, lighting candles, and praying for the missing.
The families of MH370 passengers continue to demand answers from authorities, desperate for any shred of information about their loved ones' fate.
"We just want to know what happened," Danica Weeks said, her voice heavy with emotion.
"We need closure.
We need to be able to say goodbye."
The disappearance of MH370 remains one of the biggest aviation mysteries in history.
The lack of concrete evidence and definitive answers has fueled speculation and conspiracy theories, adding another layer of pain for the grieving families.

sentences.sentence: ## Sister of Malala Shooting Suspect Renounces Brother, Offers Apology

**Peshawar, Pakistan** - The sister of Atta Ullah, the 23-year-old student being sought by authorities in connection with the shooting of Pakistani teenager Malala Yousufzai,  has publicly renounced her brother and offered a heartfelt apology to the victim.
"Please convey a message to Malala, that I apologize for what my brother did to her," Rehana Haleem said tearfully in a press conference.
"He has brought shame on our family.
I don't consider Atta Ullah my brother anymore."
Haleem's statement comes as police continue their search for Atta Ullah, who is believed to be on the run.
Malala, a champion of female education, was shot in the head by a gunman while on her way home from school on Tuesday.
She remains in critical condition, but her condition is improving according to doctors.
Haleem’s emotional appeal follows a week of national mourning and outrage over the attack.
The shooting has drawn international condemnation, with world leaders and human rights organizations calling for justice for Malala.
“I am truly sorry for what my brother has done,” Haleem continued.
“We never raised him to be violent or hateful.
We are a peace-loving family.
This action has destroyed our lives.”
While Haleem expressed deep regret for her brother’s actions, she also urged authorities to apprehend him swiftly and ensure that he faces the full consequences of his crime.
“Malala is a brave girl who only wants to learn,” she said.

sentences.sentence: ## Michael Jackson's Mom Recalls Son's Early Musical Talent on What Would Have Been His 55th Birthday

Testifying earlier in the ongoing trial, Katherine Jackson shared heartwarming stories of her son's early days, highlighting his innate musical talent and gentle nature.
Michael Jackson's life began on August 29, 1958, as the seventh child in a family crowded into a tiny home in Gary, Indiana.
His mother remembers "a sweet little child" who showed unusual empathy for others and who was "always happy."
"His first public solo was 'Climb Every Mountain' in his kindergarten program," Katherine Jackson shared, her voice brimming with pride.
"He sang it with such clarity and didn't miss – not flat or anything."
The heartwarming anecdote paints a picture of a young Michael, brimming with confidence and natural ability, already displaying the extraordinary vocal prowess that would later captivate millions.
As the trial continues, these glimpses into Michael Jackson's childhood offer a poignant reminder of the man behind the legend – a talented artist who touched the hearts of billions worldwide.
